title: Family Law Amendment (De Facto Financial Matters and Other Measures) Bill 2008

divisions.question: That this bill be now read a second time. That all words after “That” be omitted with a view to substituting the following words: “whilst not declining to give the bill a second reading, the House: (1) affirms its commitment to the central importance of the institution of marriage in Australian society; (2) recognises that partners to permanent domestic relationships other than marriage (including, but not limited to, same sex relationships) ought not to be discriminated against in relation to their financial and property affairs; and (3) notes that the Opposition has referred the bill to the Senate Legal and Constitutional Affairs Committee with a view to ensuring that, in relation to this bill: (a) the centrality of marriage is not devalued, whether by the use of inappropriate statutory language or otherwise; and (b) the rights and status of children are properly protected”. That the words proposed to be omitted ( **Ms Julie Bishop’s** amendment) stand part of the question.
That the House of Representatives be requested to make the following amendments: That the House of Representatives be requested to make the following amendment:

speeches.speaker: Stephen Conroy
speeches.brief: The bills were read a first time after a motion to proceed without formalities, take them together, and read them now was agreed to. A motion to list the bills separately on the Notice Paper will be moved after the second reading debate is adjourned.

speeches.speaker: Stephen Conroy
speeches.brief: The bill provides capital gains tax relief for private health insurance policyholders when their insurer demutualises, affecting NIB and MBF, and reverses two family trust changes from 2007 to save nearly $20 million. The second bill gives opposite-sex and same-sex de facto couples access to federal family law courts for property and maintenance matters, creating a uniform national system.

speeches.speaker: George Brandis
speeches.brief: The bill extends federal family court jurisdiction to de facto couples (same-sex and opposite-sex) for property and maintenance, with the opposition supporting it in principle but proposing amendments to preserve marriage's distinct status and to adjust parentage provisions for children of same-sex couples.

speeches.speaker: Joe Ludwig
speeches.brief: The Rudd government's bill creates a uniform federal system for de facto property and spouse maintenance, allowing de facto couples—including same-sex couples—to split superannuation and use specialist family law procedures. The speaker defended the bill against claims of endorsing polygamy, noting that four states (New South Wales, Queensland, Victoria, and Tasmania) have referred powers, and thanked the Women’s Legal Service of Australia for its contribution.

speeches.speaker: Joe Ludwig
speeches.brief: The government moved amendments to the Family Law Amendment Bill to recognise children of same-sex relationships as a "child of the relationship", allow couples separated before commencement to opt into the new property regime, and address technical issues raised by the Senate Standing Committee on Legal and Constitutional Affairs and the Law Council of Australia.

speeches.speaker: Joe Ludwig
speeches.brief: The speaker argued that the bill undermines marriage by removing its legal distinction from de facto relationships and allowing multiple concurrent de facto relationships, and Family First opposed the bill.

acts.title: Family Law Amendment (De Facto Financial Matters and Other Measures) Act 2008
